captions.detailed: This 3D model is a very thin, single-layer calibration print designed for bed leveling. It consists of a large outer rectangular frame with a crosshair intersecting at the exact center, dividing the interior into four equal quadrants. The thickness of the lines is extremely fine, designed to test first-layer adhesion and nozzle height across the build plate.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric 3D printer bed leveling test pattern in OpenSCAD. The model should generate a thin rectangular outline with central crosshairs, allowing the user to configure the overall width and depth based on different printer models, as well as the line thickness and layer height.
captions.factory: The design is built using a custom module named 'outline' that takes parameters for width (x), depth (y), height (z), and line thickness (thick). Inside this module, a translate operation centers the geometry, where a difference operation subtracts a smaller cube from a larger outer cube to create the rectangular border. Two additional thin cubes are unioned to form the horizontal and vertical crosshairs intersecting at the origin. Conditional statements select preset bed dimensions (e.g., Replicator 2, Replicator, Thingomatic) or manual inputs to pass into the outline module.
